Root cause found after Sam confirmed live testing still showed the task's in-flight tool calls/generation continuing tens of seconds to ~2 minutes after /stop reported success. internal/container/pool.go Release() always slept the configured GracePeriod and always used Docker's default ~10s graceful SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL timeout, even when the release was happening because the task's context had just been cancelled by /stop -- so a cancelled task's container (and the in-flight work inside it) could sit doing nothing for up to GracePeriod+~10s before actually dying. Fixed with a new releaseDecision(ctx, grace) helper: a cancelled ctx now skips the grace sleep entirely and requests an immediate SIGKILL (ContainerStopOptions.Timeout=0) instead of a graceful wait; a live ctx (normal completion) keeps the original behaviour byte-for-byte. Red-then-green with 3 new unit tests (internal/container/pool_test.go), task check clean, adversarially reviewed by a fresh subagent with zero blocking findings -- context-chain trace, Docker Timeout=0 semantics, and struct-equivalence for the unchanged path were all independently verified against the moby client source.

Confirmed root cause: agent containers run as root (no USER in Dockerfile, no userns-remap anywhere in docker-compose.yml/internal/container/pool.go), so a commit the agent writes to the bind-mounted worktree lands owned by UID 0 on the host. The daemon later reads those same loose objects to push, running as its own non-root host user -- 'openat objects/../..: permission denied'. Fixed: containerEnv() now passes the daemon's own os.Getuid()/os.Getgid() as WORKTREE_UID/WORKTREE_GID; hybridTrees.Push (the single choke point before the push RPC) chowns the worktree back to that owner first. Adversarial review (fresh subagent) found one real bug in the first pass -- chownTree used os.Chown, which follows symlinks and fails on a legitimately-tracked-but-dangling symlink, which would have aborted a push that would otherwise have succeeded (worse than the original bug). Fixed with os.Lchown plus a regression test proving it against a dangling symlink. Full task check clean; all other review findings (full-tree walk cost, minor test-hygiene notes) were judged non-blocking by the reviewer.

Answers: (1) in-process typed families, no out-of-process dispatch -- archie has no existing extension-process boundary and neither epic's stated payoff needs one. (2) Reaction delivery reuses internal/eventbus's Publisher/Consumer contract (PublishUnique + Ack/Nak already provide at-least-once with dedup), but NOT the existing nats.Client as-is: it hardcodes Retention: jetstream.WorkQueuePolicy (client.go:65) for the competing-consumer ARCHIE_TASKS stream, which silently starves a second consumer on overlapping subjects per CLAUDE.md's documented trap -- reactions need fan-out, so retention needs to become a Config field and reactions get their own stream. (3) Reactions in these two epics are producer-only (cheap wake via curator's WakeOnPrimaryInput pattern, or produce real work via the existing pollNATS->publishTask path) -- no veto/mutate-in-flight-work capability is being built here; that belongs to archie-core-h019 if it's ever needed. (4) No single generic Source interface -- forge intake reuses workintake.TaskEnvelope unchanged (its IdempotencyKey is already keyed on owner/repo/number, not delivery source, so a webhook-sourced envelope naturally dedups against a poll-discovered one for free); chat webhook stays internal/channels/webhook, unmodified; what's genuinely new and shared is a small cross-cutting package for HMAC/rate-limit/approval/capture mechanics, owned by neither domain.

Built internal/webhookguard: VerifyHMAC (behavior-preserving extraction from internal/channels/webhook, which now calls it instead of keeping a private copy), RateLimiter (per-source token bucket, independent budgets, observable rejection), RedactPayload (key-name heuristic matching gateway/stream.go's marker list, but -- deliberately unlike that function -- redacts only values under sensitive keys and leaves ordinary strings/numbers/bools untouched, since a captured payload exists to be inspected for field mapping in t2db.3).

Built capture storage + endpoint: docs/prds/event-capture-storage.md decides SQLite over NATS JetStream (NATS not unconditionally available pre-7d5u.2, capture's single-writer/single-reader access pattern doesn't need JetStream fan-out/replay). internal/store/captures.go adds captured_events table + InsertCapture (prune-on-write by retention age and row count) + ListCaptures. internal/webui/api_capture.go adds POST /webhooks/capture/{source}, unauthenticated (bypasses requireToken like /healthz), applying webhookguard redaction before persisting and a per-remote-address rate limit + hard body-size cap before that. New [capture] config section with documented defaults. Adversarial self-review (the usual fresh subagent pass hit a session API limit mid-run, so this was a manual re-read with the same checklist) caught and fixed three real bugs before landing: (1) body-size cap silently unenforced when unset -- added a hardcoded fallback floor since it's the only bound on a SINGLE payload's size; (2) rate limiter was keyed by the request's own unregistered source path segment, violating webhookguard.RateLimiter's documented bounded-key-space assumption -- an attacker could rotate the segment to bypass the limit and grow the bucket map unbounded; rekeyed to remote address; (3) retention prune used time.RFC3339Nano, whose variable-width trimmed fractional seconds break lexicographic string comparison in `WHERE received_at < ?` (an exact-second timestamp can sort after a later fractional one) -- switched to fixed-width RFC3339. All three have regression tests verified to fail against the pre-fix code. task check clean, golangci-lint zero new findings repo-wide.

Fixed: the live event now carries just {id, source} as a pure invalidation signal; the dashboard refetches the authoritative list. Two smaller findings (untested Data["id"] field the frontend's dedup depended on; a received_at precision mismatch between live and REST-fetched copies) were resolved as a side effect of that fix. task check clean, golangci-lint zero new findings.
